Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Hospitals Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Hospitals Inc.'s financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; Rachel Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Kim, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the Q3 2024. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue; capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion; average reimbursement rates by payer category; capital expenditure guidance for the next quarter and year; overview of key financial performance highlights; operating margin year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter; and trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes.

These areas highlight our resilience amid industry challenges like payer dynamics and volume shifts. For instance, while payer mix has tilted toward government programs, our contracting strategies are mitigating the drag. Our CapEx investments are modernizing facilities and fueling growth, with clear reimbursements supporting profitability. Financially, we're hitting strong highlights with margin expansion, and volumes are pivoting smartly to outpatient.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Dr. Reynolds. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Reynolds mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Net revenue for the Q3 2024 was $3.75 billion, an increase of 5.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix adjustments, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $3.28 billion, representing 87.5% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $2.10 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me dive deeper into these results, starting with trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue, one of the most critical dynamics shaping our financials. In our sector, payer mix defines our revenue model, encompassing the weighted average reimbursements from Medicare fee-for-service at 32%, Medicare Advantage at 18% for a total Medicare exposure of 50%, Medicaid including managed Medicaid at 22%, commercial and employer-sponsored plans at 23%, and self-pay/other at 5%. This marks a year-over-year shift of 5 points toward government payers from Q3 2023's 30% Medicare FFS, 15% MA, 20% Medicaid, 28% commercial, and 7% self-pay, with a milder 1.5-point quarter-over-quarter move from commercial into MA.

This reflects broader trends: Baby Boomers aging into Medicare, now over 65 million enrollees up 4% YoY, with MA at 52% penetration boosted by UnitedHealth's Optum and Humana in our Sun Belt markets like Florida and Texas exceeding 60%. Medicaid saw managed plans rise to 16% from 13% due to eligibility churn from pandemic unwinding, though offset by growth in programs like Georgia's Pathways, with net revenue per discharge at $8,200 versus $12,500 for commercial.

Commercial payers, our powerhouse, faced narrow networks from Blue Cross Blue Shield and CVS-Aetna, out-of-network denials up 15%, and site-neutral policies capping outpatient rates, dropping commercial NRPD to $14,200 from $15,100, a 6% decline amid VBP penalties.

Quantifying it: Same-facility admissions up 2.1% YoY to 145,000, CMI stable at 1.85 from ortho and oncology strength, but payer shifts pulled NRPA down 1.8% to $11,850. Medicare FFS steady at $10,200 per DRG-adjusted case with FY2024 IPPS 5.1% update including 2.93% wage index boost in Charlotte and Atlanta; MA at $9,800 down 2% from capitation lags. Net, mix headwinds shaved $45 million or 1.2% off our top line. Full-year, we guide 2-3 point unfavorable shift, tempering growth to 4.5-5.5% sans acquisitions.

Regionally, Southeast at 40% of beds has 55% government mix offset by Raleigh-Durham commercial premiums 20% above average; Midwest Indianapolis at 65% MA buffered by Eli Lilly plans at $12,800 NRPD; Western post-CHS tuck-ins saw 3% NRPA drag.

We're countering with contracting—75% commercial book renegotiated for 4-6% uplifts tied to quality like HCA's TCOC bundles; MA partnerships with Optum and Centene adding $150 per life via HCC coding; VBP at 35% of revenue up from 25%, Apex ACO REACH yielding $28 million shared savings offsetting 60% drag, piloting CHF/AMI bundles for 10% readmission cuts; Epic Revenue Cycle and 3M 360 at 80% facilities slashing denials to 4.2% from 7.1%, capturing $60 million, AI prior auth accelerating cash to 45 days; ASC ramp-up with 15 new sites capturing 25% ortho at 150% premiums, biosimilars boosting oncology 300 bps.

Forward, FY2025 Medicare FFS up 3.5%, MA star ratings at 4.2 could shift 1 point more, but Sun Belt growth and neuro-interventional 15% YoY position for flat to +50 bps revenue contribution, EBITDA margins to 12.5% up 75 bps.

Next, capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion. In Q3, we deployed $285 million, up 12% YoY toward full-year $1.15-$1.25 billion midpoint from $1.05 billion FY23, with 40% or $115 million maintenance at 3.5-4.0% of net PP&E aligning with HCA and Tenet.

55% or $157 million to modernization: Epic MyChart at 12 of 28 facilities for $45 million, cutting documentation 15%; $62 million for da Vinci Xi at eight hospitals totaling 22 suites, reducing prostatectomy ALOS 20% boosting CMI 0.2; $28 million Siemens AI-Rad for 25% faster reads, 10% imaging uptick; $22 million Trane HVAC/LED for LEED Silver, 18% utility cuts.

45% or $128 million expansion: $75 million Orlando 150-bed tower adding 20 ORs/40 ICUs for 15% occupancy lift in bed-short market; $35 million Indiana 75-bed micro-hospital JV with tele-ICU, HRSA grants. Pipeline $2.8 billion five-year at 12-15% IRR with 3-4% reimbursement growth.

Focused on acuity capture from 65+ growth, commercial rebound to 55%, site-neutral resilience; modeling $180 million annual EBITDA by FY26, 1-2% margin to 12.5%. Q4 at $300 million skewed expansion.

On average reimbursement rates by payer category: Consolidated net patient revenue per adjusted patient day at $2,450, up 3.2% YoY amid IPPS cuts 2.8%, No Surprises impacts, commercial talks. Mix stable 32% Medicare, 18% Medicaid, 42% managed commercial, 5% FFS indemnity, 3% self-pay.

Medicare $1,950 flat YoY +1.5% QoQ at 78% gross charges; FY24 IPPS 2.5% basket minus productivity/DSH; CDI with 3M lifting CMI 4.2% to 1.85 on heart failure/MS-DRGs; Southeast wage index edge; MA shift 15% lives yielding $18 million ACO bonuses up 25%.

Medicaid $1,720 down 1.8% from redeterminations unwinding 1.2 million lives; 65% Medicare, Texas caps; UPL $45 million Georgia/NC; Waystar denials to 9%; maternity bundles for CMI.

Commercial managed $3,280 +4.7% YoY at 150% Medicare; UHC renewal 5.2% escalators, Anthem 4.8%; Epic eligibility cutting bad debt 22%; urban premiums $3,500 vs rural $2,900; 20% VBP with Cigna $12 million savings.

Indemnity $2,950 +6%, self-pay $1,450 at 52% collections up to 68% via OmniMD, charity 2.1%.

Guide 3-5% H2 growth from FY25 IPPS 3.4%, renewals $1.2 billion, CMI 1.90 AI coding; targeting 110% commercial-to-Medicare.

Capital expenditure guidance for next quarter/year: FY2025 $750-$800 million or 7-7.5% of $10.7 billion revenue, up 15% from FY24 $650 million; 60% maintenance, 40% growth.

Q1 FY25 $180-$200 million higher front-end. Facilities 40% $300-$320 million: $120 million 250 beds Dallas/Tampa/Phoenix at 15-18% IRR, CMI to 1.95; Southeast 45%, Midwest $50 million renovations.

Equipment 30% $225-$240 million: 15 Siemens MRIs, 8 GE CTs for imaging surge; 12 da Vinci for MIS 10-15%.

Digital 20% $150-$160 million: Epic Hyperdrive $70 million FHIR; Nuance DAX $40 million AI cutting burnout 25%, Google MedLM readmissions -5%; telehealth $20 million, cyber $15 million zero-trust.

Other 10% $75-$80 million ESG retrofits 15% savings, fleet/supply.

12-14% EBITDA expansion FY26, 3.5-year payback below peers; tailwinds boomers, IPPS 2.8%, ASC double to $2.5 billion. Risks hedged.

Key financial performance highlights: Q3 net revenues $3.75 billion up 8.2% or 6.1% same-hospital ex-acquisitions; net patient $3.45 billion +9.4%. Admissions 145,000 flat, CMI +2.3% to 1.92 ortho/cardio; days +1.8% to 785,000; outpatient procedures +15.7%, ASCs 28% volume.

Payer: commercial 48% +11%, Medicare 38%, Medicaid 11%. EBITDA $512 million +12.5% margins 18.0% +110 bps; rev/adm $18,400 +7.9%; labor +5.1% vacancy to 8%; Vizient $25 million supply; GLP-1 controlled.

GAAP op income $285 million 10.0%; adj net $210 million EPS $1.52 +14%; FCF $320 million, repurchases $150 million, CapEx $120 million. Liquidity $2.1 billion, leverage 2.8x; $450 million Coastal acquisition accretive.

Sunbelt 65% growth +9.8%; Epic Phase 2 95% interop denials -15%; telehealth 450,000 +22%. Q4 rev $3.78-$3.85 billion EBITDA $535-$555 million; FY rev $11.5-$11.7 billion margins 17.8-18.2%.

Operating margins 12.5% +70 bps QoQ from 11.8%, +230 bps YoY from 10.2%. YoY: rev +4.2% adm +6.1% RPAA +2.8%; inpatient +5.3%, outpatient +8.2% 12 ASCs; supply -7.1% Vizient, labor +3.8% Flex Workforce contract to 7%; ACO 28% Medicare readmits -1.6%.

Regional: Northeast 14.2% +310 bps commercial 48%; Midwest 10.8% +150; Southwest 13.7% Medicaid +9%. QoQ: CMI +2.1% to 1.68, RCM AI AR 42 days collections +11%, non-labor -1.2%.

M&A Tenet $250 million, Epic AI scribing -25% doc time, UHC bundles. Q4 12.7-13.1%.

Finally, trends in inpatient vs. outpatient volumes. Inpatient admissions 142,000 -2.1% YoY like HCA/Tenet; days 782,000 -1.2%, ALOS 5.51 from 5.62, CMI 1.78. Outpatient visits 2.47 million +6.8%, procedures 1.12 million, REPD $1.45 billion +8.2%, 62% mix from 58%.

Inpatient drivers: MA 32% auths -4% ortho; ALOS pneumonia -0.8 SNF; COVID down 15%. Outpatient: GI +12%, ASCs 28 JVs $420 million +15% 25% margins site-neutral.

Sunbelt flat inpatient 42% commercial, outpatient +9.2% Miami spine +18%; Northeast inpatient -4.5% Medicaid, outpatient +5.1% tele 180,000 +22%.

Strategy: $450 million CapEx 5 ASCs ortho/cardio/ENT; Epic/Health Catalyst +7% conversion 2,500 chole; 15 BCBS bundles readmits 2.1%; RN 82%. Back half inpatient -1%, outpatient 7-9%. 55/45 mix resilient.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Chen for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Heart Failure Care Coordination Program has shown promising results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform and remote patient monitoring programs.

Following that, Tom Hargrove will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including supply chain consortium partnerships and AI-driven staff scheduling, which have resulted in significant cost savings and improved patient flow.

Next, Rachel Patel will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Rachel Patel:
Thank you, Tom. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets and enhance our service offerings.

After that, David Kim will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

David Kim:
Thank you, Rachel. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

David Kim:
Good morning, John. Recent cybersecurity threats, like the Change Healthcare incident, haven't materially impacted our operations thanks to our proactive measures. We've invested $15 million this quarter in zero-trust architecture, multi-factor authentication across all systems, and regular penetration testing. Our Epic EHR remains fully segregated, with no patient data breaches. Downtime was minimal at under 4 hours during a phishing simulation, and we're compliant with HITRUST and HIPAA. This fortifies us against ransomware, ensuring continuity in care delivery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Emily. We're aggressively expanding telehealth and RPM, with $20 million in CapEx this year. Virtual visits hit 450,000, up 22%, handling 25% behavioral health and funneling 30% to outpatient. New hybrid ORs enable remote proctoring, and RPM via Philips tele-ICU targets 5% readmission cuts. Partnerships with Teladoc for stroke and Zoom/Azure integration aim for 18% of encounters virtual by FY25, boosting access in rural sites and capturing Medicare Advantage upside.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

Rachel Patel:
Absolutely, Mike. Our partnerships are core to growth. Recent JVs with SCA Health for 28 ASCs yield 25% margins, adding $420 million revenue. Optum and Centene for MA risk-adjustment add $150 per life; Teladoc tele-stroke; Intuitive for robotics. UHC/Anthem VBP covers 35% revenue, $28 million ACO savings. These drive 15-18% IRR expansions like Orlando tower, offsetting mix shifts with 10% readmission wins and CMI uplift, targeting $2.5 billion ambulatory by 2027.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Hospitals Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
